review.alternative: Responsibility distribution problems may stem primarily from legal frameworks rather than epistemic opacity among actors.
review.would_change_mind: Demonstration of clear deterministic accountability attribution in multi-developer AI deployments.

claims.statement: Responsibility attribution in AI systems is complicated by distributed involvement across development and deployment pipelines.

support.explanation: Coeckelbergh highlights how collective technological action involving multiple actors complicates knowledge and responsibility distribution.
support.passage:
Users of AI and indeed managers or regula-
tors may not always know who else is or has been involved in the development and
use of the technology, and what they have been doing and intending. This renders
responsible use and responsibility attribution and distribution difficult.

review.alternative: Delayed evaluative feedback can still be fully traced back to initial static loss specifications without creating novel agency.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that delayed evaluative feedback carries identical accountability properties to standard supervised target labels.

claims.statement: Autonomous decision-making architectures rely on sequential feedback loops that separate specific system actions from direct human design inputs.

support.explanation: Sequential decision-making frameworks operate on evaluative and delayed feedback rather than direct static human instruction.
support.passage:
Unlike traditional su-
pervised learning methods that usually rely on one-shot, ex-
haustive and supervised reward signals, RL tackles with se-
quential decision making problems with sampled, evaluative
and delayed feedback simultaneously.

actions.findings:
Responsibility attribution in AI systems is complicated by distributed involvement across development and deployment pipelines. [source-51056065f1394913]

Autonomous decision-making architectures rely on sequential feedback loops that separate specific system actions from direct human design inputs. [source-89092a29a3e14897]
actions.limitations: Analysis relies on conceptual ethics literature and general reinforcement learning surveys; specific empirical attribution frameworks require further formalization.
actions.next_questions: How can formal accountability frameworks delineate moral and operational responsibility when autonomous agents adapt iteratively through environment feedback?

proposal.summary: Synthesized available literature on responsibility attribution in artificial intelligence systems, examining how distributed involvement across development and adaptive decision-making mechanisms complicate accountability.
